references.text: The first time the difference between Esau and Jacob is mentioned, Esau is described as hairy at birth.
Describes the personalities and lifestyles of Esau and Jacob, highlighting the differences between the two brothers.
Rebekah placed the skins of the young goats on Jacob's hands and on the smooth part of his neck to imitate Esau's hairy skin.
Isaac notes the difference in voice but is deceived by Jacob's appearance, which has been altered to resemble Esau's hairy skin.
Rebekah's awareness of the brothers' differences (27:11) prepares her intervention when Esau plans murder (27:42).
Isaac's doubt about identity based on hands (27:22) directly confirms Jacob's fear regarding the skin difference mentioned in 27:11.
Isaac's request to feel the hands (27:21) is the direct challenge to Jacob's fear of the skin difference in 27:11.
Jacob's claimed identity as Esau (27:19) is the direct result of his concern about the skin difference in 27:11.
Malachi interprets the brotherhood theologically (God's choice) and gives deeper meaning to the physical difference in 27:11.
Describes Esau's physical nature ('red') as a parallel to the 'hairy' skin in 27:11, emphasizing how physical traits define the brothers' destinies.
Esau's rage (27:41) is the direct consequence of the deception made possible by the skin difference in 27:11.
